provider.name: Transport for London (JamCams)
provider.description: TfL publishes its road traffic cameras — 'JamCams' — as open data through the TfL Unified API, exposing a regularly refreshed still image and a five-second looped video per camera. The feeds exist so that developers can use them in their own services, which makes this the clearest example in the registry of a feed that was intentionally published rather than merely reachable.
provider.licence: TfL open data terms — worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to copy, publish, distribute, adapt and exploit the data commercially and non-commercially
provider.attribution: Powered by TfL Open Data. Contains OS data © Crown copyright and database rights. Geomni UK Map data © and database rights.
provider.rateLimitNotes: TfL's terms state a maximum of 500 calls per minute per data feed. Metadata refresh must stay well inside that ceiling; we never fetch the image bytes server-side at all.

cameras.name: Piccadilly Circus
cameras.locationLabel: Piccadilly Circus, City of Westminster, London
cameras.embedNotes: Permitted. The TfL transport data service terms grant a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, non-exclusive licence to copy, publish, distribute and transmit the information, to adapt it, and to exploit it commercially and non-commercially, including combining it with other information in your own products. Attribution is mandatory and must include 'Powered by TfL Open Data' together with the Ordnance Survey Crown copyright notice. Terms fetched and read 2026-08-31. The embed is click-to-load: the reader's browser connects to the TfL S3 bucket only on an explicit click, and we never proxy the image.
